title: Gender (Still) Matters in Business School
eligible_reason: Treatment is instructor gender interacted with student gender within course-term cells. No unit-specific adoption dates, so there is no staggered-adoption design.
design_notes: Equation 3 (Table 6) is described as a difference-in-differences specification: grade_ictgs on female instructor and female instructor x female student, with term x course x student-gender fixed effects, student-term controls interacted with subject and instructor-term controls interacted with student gender. Administrative grades for 6,312 undergraduates (2005-2018 graduating cohorts). Table 6 col 1 N = 48,498. Cols 2-4 use survey data (N = 851-864) with course x student-gender FE. SEs clustered at course-instructor. Treatment is non-absorbing, repeatedly reassigned across courses, and not an adoption event.
screener_notes: Not eligible: no adoption-date design, time-varying controls. Data are confidential administrative records from a U.S. Midwest public university business school plus authors' survey. No replication package was listed in the batch file (package_dir and regressions_path empty); screening is from the article text only.
